items.title: Putting sign language AI into users’ hands
items.summary: Introducing sign-language-to-text (SL2T), our breakthrough model powering new sign language features for Deaf and hard of hearing users.
items.content:
Google DeepMind Sign Language Team

Introducing sign-language-to-text (SL2T), our breakthrough model powering new sign language features for Deaf and hard of hearing users.

AI's ability to process spoken languages has advanced rapidly over recent decades, enabling automatic translation, dictation, and conversational interfaces that feel effortless to hearing users. Yet this technological revolution has not reached the world’s more than 200 sign languages — and the estimated 70 million Deaf and hard of hearing people who use them.

Today, we’re introducing a massively multilingual sign-language-to-text (SL2T) translation model that marks a breakthrough in quality and generality. With it, we are bringing sign language AI out of the lab and into consumer products for the first time: SL2T powers sign-to-text dictation in Gboard and Live Transcribe on Pixel 11 , starting with American Sign Language (ASL) to English. More devices are coming soon, and additional languages will follow.

Similarly to how hearing users can use dictation to speak instead of typing, this feature enables Deaf users to sign to their phone anywhere they’d normally type. You can sign to search the web, draft messages or documents, and ask Gemini to solve queries or execute tasks. In Live Transcribe, you can sign responses in conversations instead of having to type back and forth. According to our testers, signing in ASL is faster, more natural, and more delightful than typing in English.

Sign languages are the primary languages of Deaf communities around the world and the cornerstone of Deaf cultural identity. There is great diversity among deaf people in terms of their level of proficiency in signing, speaking, reading, and writing, so it is important to support access in all modalities. Deaf people can benefit from sign language processing in the same way that hearing people benefit from spoken language processing, plus the technology opens new possibilities for bridging the communication gap between Deaf and hearing communities. Despite this opportunity for positive social impact, progress in sign language AI has been slow — both because building AI for sign languages presents complex challenges and because widespread misconceptions exist about how the languages themselves work.

Compared to spoken language transcription, sign language translation presents two core challenges. First, transcribing speech is a matter of performing a sequential mapping from sound to text in the same language, whereas sign languages are independent, natural languages with their own distinct grammars and lexicons. As a result, they require true machine translation rather than a sequential process of sign-to-word transformations. Second, the model must learn to “see” and understand physical movement. Sign languages convey meaning through simultaneous movements of the hands, arms, torso, head, and face. Accurately tracking these at high frame rates is a difficult and computationally demanding computer vision task.

Given this background, it is easy to understand why some early attempts at sign language technology, like sign language gloves, were fundamentally limited: sign languages aren't simply “English on the hands.” They require complex visual perception of fine-grained whole-body movements and full-fledged language translation. SL2T is designed to deliver both.

SL2T sees sign language inputs as points on the signer's body and translates them into streaming text outputs. Example from the FLEURS-ASL benchmark.

We built SL2T by combining a user-centric, culturally informed approach with massive data scaling. The model is trained on over 100,000 hours of data across more than 50 sign languages — with roughly a quarter of the data in ASL. Training jointly on diverse languages, dialects, and proficiency levels causes the model to learn shared underlying structures, outperforming single-language models in our experiments.

To protect user privacy, SL2T sees sign language as a sequence of pose landmark locations rather than a raw camera feed. An on-device model ( MediaPipe Holistic ) tracks the location of points on the signer, and only these geometric coordinates are sent to the server for translation, allowing the original video to be discarded immediately.

SL2T translates this coordinate sequence directly into text, bypassing intermediate annotations known as “glosses” that are widely used in prior work on sign language translation. Glosses fail to capture rich, non-linear aspects of sign languages such as non-manual markers and spatial constructions. Translating directly from landmarks removes artificial vocabulary limits and allows translation quality to scale directly with data.

SL2T is the most capable sign language translation model to date according to key benchmarks like FLEURS-ASL (sd-test), which assesses ASL to English translation quality. SL2T achieves a remarkable zero-shot score of 70 BLEURT, which is significantly higher than any previously reported score. But optimizing academic benchmarks alone doesn’t guarantee usability in real-world applications, so we worked hard on practical issues like minimizing streaming latency, preventing hallucination on non-signing inputs, ensuring fairness for the 10% of signers who are left-handed, and improving performance for one-handed signing, which is used while holding a smartphone in the other hand.

Examples from the FLEURS-ASL benchmark. SL2T accurately translates complex ASL into fluent English. Occasional errors remain in rare signs, rapid fingerspelling ("prey" → "grey"), passive constructions, classifier depictions (dropping "claws"), and tense without context ("kicked off" → "start").

items.title: Google’s Pixel 11 lineup offer fewer hardware changes, but much more Gemini
items.summary: Google Pixel 11 Series starts $100 costlier than the last year, but offers 256GB base storage
items.content:
For the last few years, Google’s Pixel has been a showcase of new AI features, with few hardware changes from the previous year’s devices. Similarly, the Pixel 11 series isn’t too different in design and internals from its predecessor.

However, this year’s devices have more Gemini features to complete tasks in the background, including a new Wispr Flow-like transcription feature, a live translation feature that works across content, and a new camera feature that captures the right frames.

With this year’s Pixel 11 series launch, Google is thinking more agentic AI to complete your tasks. With Gemini, U.S.-based users will be able to order groceries, book rides, or get coffee, for instance. Plus, Gemini can call businesses on users’ behalf for table reservations or appointments. Google said that users can take over or stop tasks at any point in time and also review transcripts for AI-operated calls.

The company has also evolved the “Magic Cue” feature from last year to use Gemini, which proactively surfaces contextual information, to now display information from across your apps to help you find suggestions for things like a dinner spot or show.

In May, Google announced a dictation product called Rambler to take on competitors like Wispr Flow and Aqua. Now, that product is making its way to the Pixel phones.

The new Pixel series phones have some other helpful features that might be handy for daily usage, too. First, the device can translate videos, podcasts, and voice messages in the target language. The company is also making its “Circle to Search” gesture-based feature available directly in the camera, something that Apple also did in iOS 27 by making Siri available in the camera .

What’s more, Google is adding an accessibility feature to the camera, which uses Gemini to translate sign language into text to help people communicate with others who have hearing impairments. And the company has redesigned the live transcribe interface for improved communication.

Google also added a few AI tricks embedded into its camera. One feature is called “Magic Capture,” which picks the best frames out of hundreds of frames it captures between when users press start and end. The idea is to take a video and get photos as a byproduct. Google said that the feature also auto-crops and unblurs the frames to make them ready for sharing.

The company has upgraded its super zoom from 100x to 120x for Pro phones, and from 20x to 30x for the base Pixel 11. With the new devices, users will be able to create custom looks for the camera, which are specialized filters that appear when users are snapping images.

The Pro phones are also getting faster capture with a feature called “Instant Night Sight,” which takes 4.5x less time than the previous-gen phone’s Night Sight. Google enhanced video shooting, too, with support for 8K resolution with video boost and better stability.

For creators, Google added a “creator suite” mode in video settings, which lets you use Pixel 11 devices as a teleprompter while shooting clips. When you are done shooting, the clip is saved in a dedicated folder, making it easier to find for editing.

All the Pixel phones now run the latest Tensor G6 processor, which has 20% better power efficiency and allows for 25% faster browsing, as per Google. Plus, it lets users take faster low-light photos with Night Sight Instant.

The new image signal processing on the chip also enables 120x magic zoom on the Pixel 11 Pro XL. The company said that the new processors run the latest models with lower latency, but didn’t offer any specific metrics.

The display size on all phones is the same, but the Pro models get a slightly brighter display, which could be helpful in the daylight.

Google said Pro models get an updated main camera sensor that takes higher-quality photos than the previous generation without specifying any numbers. It also said the new telephoto sensor allows for 32% more light while capturing an image.

London-based startup Nothing made its phones recognizable by Glyph bars and then a Glyph interface. Google is not that extravagant, but it has now placed an LED light on the back, which is built around the flashlight. This acts as an indicator for calls or messages from favorite contacts when Gemini is thinking or listening.

All these devices are available to pre-order starting today and will start with a base storage of 256GB.

The Pixel 11 starts at $899, the 11 Pro starts at $1,099, and the 11 Pro XL starts at $1,299. (The prices of the Pixel 11 and the Pixel 11 Pro are the same as last year’s 256GB models, but you could buy a 128 GB model at that time with a $100 lower price tag.)

With the rising prices of components, the company has bumped the price of the top model by $100 compared to the Pixel 10 XL.

A new lineup of Pixel 11 accessories is also arriving alongside the phones, including new Pixelsnap cases (which now include clear) and Pixelsnap Ring Stand colors.

items.title: Google unveils the Pixel Watch 5 with a smarter Gemini and advanced health monitoring
items.summary: The new smartwatch, which starts at $399, can track blood pressure patterns and insulin resistance, as well as deliver personalized help and better sleep tracking.
items.content:
At its Made by Google event on Wednesday, Google unveiled the Pixel Watch 5 with a smarter Gemini experience, as well as advanced fitness and health monitoring. The new smartwatch, which starts at $399, can track blood pressure patterns and insulin resistance, as well as deliver personalized help and better sleep tracking.

Google says it’s designed the watch to deliver personalized and proactive help right when it’s needed. For example, the watch will proactively suggest relevant actions or information based on a text message’s context, like instantly pulling up a smoothie place your sister sent you.

You can raise your wrist to ask Gemini a question, handle requests like finding a nearby lunch spot with navigation, or use Gemini offline to manage timers, alarms, and workouts with your voice.

The watch will also dynamically surface timely updates right at the bottom of the watch face, like flight info, ETAs, and other helpful reminders.

As for the new health features, the tech giant says the smartwatch uses sensors and machine learning to track blood pressure patterns before they can put strain on your heart. Google says the feature was tested against 24-hour blood pressure monitors and uses an advanced waveform model trained on more than 1 billion minutes of data from over 500,000 people.

The insulin resistance feature is designed to identify changes in metabolic health that may be associated with insulin resistance and an increased risk of developing prediabetes or type 2 diabetes. The feature combines signals from sleep, heart rate, physical activity, and other health data. A large sensor model then analyzes these signals over time to identify long-term changes in insulin resistance.

Google will give users a summary of their blood pressure and insulin resistance trends every month.

There’s also a new feature that can detect a persistent drop in oxygen saturation and will contact emergency services if the watch determines that a breathing emergency may be occurring. This feature is launching in select European countries before expanding to additional regions.

Additionally, the watch’s sleep-stage tracking is 15% more accurate and there’s also a new bedtime watch face that reduces nighttime distractions. A new “Smart Wake” feature wakes users at an optimal point in their sleep cycle, while a new sleep breathing quality metric tracks minute-by-minute changes in blood oxygen levels.

As for fitness, Google says the Pixel Watch 5 delivers its most accurate GPS route tracking yet, with route mapping that’s two times more accurate than previous generations. The improved accuracy is designed to provide users with more precise workout and running data, including a closer match between your recorded route and the actual course.

The Pixel Watch 5 features the Qualcomm Snapdragon W5 Gen 2 platform and has 12% more CPU performance and 50% more RAM than the previous platform. Google says the Watch 5 is 20% faster overall.

The Pixel Watch five supports up to 40 hours of battery life and is available in new colors, including Canyon Fog and Olive. The 41mm version starts at $399, while the 44mm starts at $429. The smartwatch is available for pre-order starting Wednesday and will be available on August 20.

items.title: Google takes on AirTag with the new $29 Pixel Tag
items.summary: Google’s new Pixel Tag taps into its Find Hub network to help users track lost keys, bags, and other items.
items.content:
Alongside its announcement of a new lineup of Pixel 11 smartphones, Google on Wednesday introduced its answer to Apple’s AirTag. At its livestreamed “ Made by Google ’26 ” event, the company unveiled a new product designed for keeping track of your valuable items: the $29 Google Pixel Tag.

Similar to how Apple’s AirTag leverages its network of iPhones to find lost devices, the new Pixel Tag taps uses Google’s Find Hub network, which taps into Android devices around the world. Android users can add the tag to their phone’s built-in Android Find Hub, which is already used to help users find their lost Android smartphones and other devices, similar to Apple’s Find My.

Helpfully, you can locate and ring your Pixel Tag directly from your Pixel Watch, too, not just your phone.

Where the Pixel Tag differs from AirTag is in its look and feel.

Apple’s lost-item finder is small, round, and engravable; Google opted for a slimmer, elongated device instead. Spec-by-spec, the Pixel Tag is 1.1 inches wide, compared to the AirTag’s 1.26 inches. As the Pixel Tag is oval-shaped, it’s 1.8 inches high from top to bottom. Thickness-wise, the Pixel Tag clocks in at a depth of 0.2 inches, compared with the AirTag’s 0.31 inches (which Apple calls its height).

By weight, the two competitors are comparable, as the Pixel Tag weighs 0.4 ounces with the battery, and the AirTag comes in at 0.39 oz.

Both are also rated IP67 for splash, water, and dust resistance, meaning they can withstand submersion in a maximum depth of 1 meter for up to 30 minutes.

Designed to be attached to items like keychains and bags, the Pixel Tag will cost $29 for a one-pack and $99 for a four-pack when it becomes available for purchase on November 11, 2026.

items.title: Google’s new Pixel 11 Pro Fold offers a stronger build and brighter screens
items.summary: The Pixel 11 Pro Fold will cost $1,899
items.content:
Samsung’s short and wide foldable is the talk of the town, but Google is not experimenting with its design with today’s unveiling of the new Pixel 11 Fold, which appears largely unchanged on the outside. The company said that the new foldable is stronger and lighter than the previous-gen phone, but it’s also costlier.

Google said that it developed a new, stronger hinge for this year’s Pixel 11 Pro Fold . It’s also adding a Super Actua display to the outer display with 3,600 nits of peak brightness. Both the inner and outer displays are 20% brighter than its predecessor, according to the company.

There is a bit of a battery downgrade, however, as it now offers a 4,750 mAh capacity battery instead of 5,015 mAh from last year’s model. On the plus side, this is probably the reason why the phone is 1mm thinner and roughly 20 grams lighter.

Another small upgrade on the charging front is that the new foldable supports 25W wireless charging.

The Pixel 11 Pro Fold is getting an updated 48-megapixel sensor that pulls in more light for more detailed photos in different lighting conditions. Because of the new G6 Tensor chip and the updated image processor, the phone can digitally zoom at 30x, up from 20x.

The device will be available in both the Olive and Obsidian colors, and will cost $1,899.

items.title: Google’s Pixel 11 series pairs a little new hardware with a lot of new software
items.summary: When I first picked up the Pixel 11 Pro this week, it was clear to me that this was one of those refinement years - at least when it comes to hardware. Aesthetically, the phones are as beautiful as ever, with Google's signature camera bar and bright, colorful backing glass. There
items.content:
More helpful features, less AI slop.

When I first picked up the Pixel 11 Pro this week, it was clear to me that this was one of those refinement years — at least when it comes to hardware. Aesthetically, the phones are as beautiful as ever, with Google’s signature camera bar and bright, colorful backing glass. There are small updates, like a single piece of glass covering the camera bar and the all-new HiLight ambient LED on the Pros. But this year, the Pixel is all about quality of life and software improvements.

After weeks of teasers, Google has finally formally announced the Pixel 11, Pixel 11 Pro, Pixel 11 Pro XL, and Pixel 11 Pro Fold. The phones are all shipping next week, on August 20th, and Google is holding a splashy event the evening of August 12th to show off the devices. Ahead of that, we had a chance to take a first look at everything that’s coming up.

Let’s start with the bad news up front: All of these phones are $100 more expensive than last year’s. Google has killed off the 128GB base storage option this year, which means the Pixel 11 now starts at $899 for a 256GB model. All storage tiers still come with 12GB of RAM, but the higher entry price is no doubt driven by RAMageddon, which has been increasing costs across the industry.

If you can look past the price, you’ll find a refined version of last year’s phone that looks and feels a bit more premium. The camera bar is now made of a singular piece of glass and is over 40 percent thinner. If you use it with one of Google’s cases, the bar will become completely flush. (This gives you three different camera bar thickness options on the Pixel line now, which only get thicker the more premium you go.)

The cameras have been upgraded, too. On the Pixel 11, the 48MP wide is quoted with 56 percent more light gathering capability from its new 1/1.56-inch sensor, and the 5x telephoto lens can now digitally zoom up to 30x, which Google says is enabled by the new image signal processor in the Tensor G6 chipset. And considering the new Tensor G6 chip is said to be up to 20 percent more efficient, Google is quoting up to 30-plus hours of battery life across the lineup.

Perhaps the most interesting update to me is the new Camera Looks feature. You can think of this similarly to the film recipes on Fujifilm cameras, presenting users with stylized presets that can be customized to their liking.

What makes Camera Looks so interesting, though, is instead of just being a filter on top of the preprocessed Pixel photo, the phone will process the photo completely differently at the sensor level depending on which settings you choose, potentially using less frame stacking and sharpening to deliver the photo you actually want. During my briefing at least, this really delivered. The Natural mode does an amazing job of lowering the sharpness and contrast and making the photos look much more true to life, and I’m excited to take it for a proper spin later. If you want to learn more about this, check out my dedicated article where I spoke with Pixel camera lead Isaac Reynolds .

Another new feature inside the camera is Magic Capture. This is a camera mode alongside the photo and video modes that creates a sort of hybrid mashup of the two, where the phone will automatically pick out short clips and images you can share. During my hands-on time this feature didn’t work great, only giving me one small clip and one photo from a roughly 15-second recording, but I believe it’s meant for longer clips at things like kids’ birthday parties. We’ll have to test this in the field once we have more time with the device.

Google is also adding a new Creator Suite inside the camera, which gives you access to tools like social media framing guides, speech enhancement, a teleprompter, and automatic folder structures for video. I was surprised to see this so deeply integrated into the camera itself, and it’s clear Google is going after a new audience and hoping to make the Pixel the best phone for small creators.

The phones also all feature Qi2.2 — an upgrade from Qi2 last year. Google says this offers 25 percent faster wireless charging of up to 25W, an upgrade from the 15W max the Pixel 10 offered. However, many users reported seeing a maximum wireless charge rate of only 5W with the Pixel 10 when using older chargers, so hopefully the problem is fixed this year.

The Pixel 11 will come in purple, green, black, and an extremely hot magenta.

The 11 Pro and Pro XL are where things get a little more interesting this year. Like the standard Pixel 11, they start at 256GB of storage and 12GB of RAM (down from 16GB last year), which starts at $1,099. If you’re a power user, you can still get 16GB of RAM if you buy the 512GB or 1TB models.

You’re definitely getting more with the Pro models this year, though. The display on the Pixel 11 Pro gets up to a super bright 3,600 nits, which Google says is the brightest display ever on a smartphone. This isn’t a massive difference from the 3,300-nit peak brightness from last year, but it’s something for your money.

The main camera sensor on the Pixel 11 Pro has been improved, with a new 50MP model that Google says uses less power and should perform better in the 1x-to-5x zoom range. There’s also a new 48MP telephoto lens with a larger 1/1.95-inch sensor that delivers a quoted 30 percent improvement in light sensitivity. And just like the standard Pixel 11, the 11 Pro has a further zoom range, now extending up to 120x, which Google says is enabled by the ISP in Tensor G6.

items.title: Google is making the Pixel cameras better by making them worse
items.summary: If you look at a photo taken by a smartphone today, it's hard to find much that's technically wrong. Faces are bright and visible. The skies are pristine and blue. Even at night, scenes are well lit and noise-free. If the physical limitations of a tiny camera are what you're tryi
items.content:
Google’s new Camera Looks feature will do less computational photography — and that’s a great thing.

If you look at a photo taken by a smartphone today, it’s hard to find much that’s technically wrong . Faces are bright and visible. The skies are pristine and blue. Even at night, scenes are well lit and noise-free. If the physical limitations of a tiny camera are what you’re trying to solve for, you could probably label smartphone photography a mostly solved problem.

But in our current moment, the photos people are drawn to are not flawless — and that’s created a real problem for the people making smartphone cameras. “The gap between what two random people want from their camera is growing dramatically,” says Isaac Reynolds, who leads the Pixel camera team at Google. Some people want a perfectly optimized photo, Reynolds says. “But there’s a growing number of people who want something that they feel is more authentic or traditional, by their definition.”

That’s what Reynolds and the Pixel team are setting out to solve with Camera Looks, a total rethink of how the camera captures and styles an image on the Pixel 11 series. The phones include a new suite of processing tools aimed at giving people much more control over the camera’s output. At first glance, they look a lot like filters, with names like Black Tie, Classic, and most strikingly, Digi, in reference to the growing trend of buying cheap digital cameras from the early aughts. But unlike a filter, which generally applies editing tweaks after the processing happens, Camera Looks is changing how image data is processed at the sensor level.

“The pipeline spans the entire system,” Reynolds says. “It’s inside HDR Plus. It’s inside the processing engine. It’s inside the camera app as well in how we make certain decisions about auto exposure and integration time and number of frames packaged and captured.”

In the last decade or so, smartphone cameras have been engineered to do battle with the limitations of physics using what’s known as “computational photography.” Too dark? Night mode uses multi-frame image stacking to brighten the photo without adding too much noise. Need to zoom in but don’t have a telephoto lens? An on-device model can artificially create data it expects to be in your photo. Too small of a sensor for natural blur? Phones can use subject segmentation to recognize objects, cut out the subject, and emulate depth of field.

The result has been crisp, clear photos — and also a lot of (mostly younger) consumers carrying around old iPhones and cheap point-and-shoots from the early aughts to get a simpler, less processed, and (to their eye) better look.

“If you are looking for a minimal look … we simply don’t do the processing at all.”

The Pixel 11’s new Camera Looks feature is Google’s response to this growing trend. And to solve it, the Pixel team is allowing users to dial back how much processing happens when they snap a shot. Some of the Pixel’s Camera Looks will merge fewer frames together, leaving the highlights a bit blown out instead of compressing them to a midtone. Some of them won’t apply as much sharpening and will instead leave the image softer on the edges. You could argue that these new photos are technically “worse” — with reduced detail and dynamic range — but the result should be a photo closer to what any given user actually wants. This is a completely different way of thinking about computational photography, using tools to optimize for style instead of for technical perfection.

Until now, the Pixel camera pipeline has done the same type of processing for every user, and any edits to match their preferred style had to be made after the fact. But when an image is already fully processed, you’re stuck with the data and artifacts caused by that processing. “Once you’ve processed it that way, you can’t do less. If there was a merge artifact, that is baked in. It’s irreversible,” Reynolds says. With the Pixel 11, “we bring it a lot earlier, and that way if you are looking for a minimal look, which is minimally processed, we simply don’t do the processing at all.”

This, I think, is the most Google way to handle this change in camera mindset I could have imagined. In order to keep people from being too confused about technical jargon like tone compression or frame merging, Google is intelligently making processing decisions for you based on style selections most users can understand — and more importantly, can see. Reynolds tells me that there were long debates inside the camera team for just how many sliders users should have access to, and they landed on more than you’d probably expect. “ There are so many in there that I actually had to have an escalation meeting with my PM and my UX team about how many controls we were allowed to put in there,” Reynolds says. “There’s a lot of controls that photographers say are critical to have. We had a lot of trouble cutting it down.” For every Camera Look, you’ll get a set of six or more different levers, like contrast, warmth, tint, and saturation. And some Looks, like the black-and-white look Black Tie, will give you extra options, like red, green, and blue filters, which darken certain frequencies of light on black-and-white film.

This is notably different from the way Apple is currently thinking about cameras on the iPhone. Since the iPhone 13, Apple has included “Photographic Styles” in its camera — a series of presets that users can dial in through only two settings, tone and color (brightness/contrast and saturation). Google gives you access to these settings, too, but you’re also getting access to computational settings like sharpness and grain, which can more dramatically tune the look of your image before you shoot.

items.title: Google’s Pixel Watch 5 dives deeper into AI and health
items.summary: The $399 Google Pixel Watch 5 isn't about the hardware. Sure, there's a new satin pyrite case finish, a few new strap colors, and a Steph Curry Special Edition. Under the hood, there's a slightly faster Qualcomm processor and an itty-bitty battery bump. There's a $50 price hike f
items.content:
We’re talking offline Gemini, proactive AI suggestions, better GPS maps, insulin resistance trends, and a $50 price hike.

The $399 Google Pixel Watch 5 isn’t about the hardware. Sure, there’s a new satin pyrite case finish, a few new strap colors, and a Steph Curry Special Edition. Under the hood, there’s a slightly faster Qualcomm processor and an itty-bitty battery bump. There’s a $50 price hike from last year, too, because the Pixel Watch 5 isn’t immune to RAMageddon — none of us are. Otherwise, no one would blame you for looking at this watch and thinking absolutely nothing’s changed. That’s because the big updates this year are all software-based.

This isn’t a huge surprise considering Google’s Fitbit Air launch in May. And after seeing some Pixel Watch 5 demos, it’s clear this year’s refresh is furthering the AI and proactive health themes that Google introduced earlier this year.

Health and fitness features account for the bulk of the updates, but Gemini on the wrist gets a few key improvements. You can now use it offline for simple tasks like starting timers and launching apps. (Though I noticed in my demo it was notably slower when doing this offline.) Gemini will also be more proactive in making suggestions. One example I saw: a text asking for my availability brought up the option to check Google Calendar from the wrist. Likewise, there’s now an icon right on the watchface that surfaces real-time information for things like timers, Uber ETAs, and workouts. Meanwhile, the pinchy pinch and wrist-flick features came via a software update to Pixel Watches in December , but they’re much more fully integrated into the UI with WearOS 7.

You can also use AI to generate watchfaces. I created a watchface featuring “fat cats and an elegant font.” It didn’t quite do that. The fat cats weren’t characters, so much as pleasantly plump, cat-shaped clock numbers. It’s a gimmicky way to shoehorn the Nano Banana model onto the watch… but if that’s your thing, it works.

Now for the health stuff. The most novel update is Breathing Emergency Detection. It’s an extension of last year’s Loss of Pulse feature. When the watch detects a severe drop in blood oxygen saturation (aka SpO2), it’ll trigger a call to emergency services and your designated emergency contacts. (A sudden drop in SpO2 may indicate you’re struggling to breathe.) To minimize false positives, the watch uses a combination of heart rate, motion, and altitude sensors. While I didn’t get to see the feature in action, I was told at my demo that the feature won’t kick in unless SpO2 drops to roughly 83 percent — so a significant decrease — for an extended period. It also disables once the watch determines you’ve been asleep for 30 minutes to mitigate false alarms linked to low SpO2 from sleep apnea or side sleeping. The feature also isn’t intended to be used by people with preexisting or chronic respiratory conditions; it’s more for flagging acute instances where a person may have stopped breathing. It’ll be available on both the Pixel Watch 4 and 5 in Europe at launch, and is pending clearance from the FDA in the US.

A less high-stakes feature is that the Pixel Watch (and Fitbit Air) will also track nightly sleep breathing quality and provide monthly updates. The idea is to see how your daily trends impact respiratory health at night over a longer time frame.

Two other health features are Blood Pressure Trends and Insulin Resistance Trends. First and foremost: Neither of these is diagnostic. Both are wellness features intended to function as “check engine light”-type warnings, require a minimum of a week’s worth of data, and flag trends monthly. They won’t be available right when the Pixel Watch 5 launches; rollout is currently scheduled for September. That said, these features will also come to the Pixel Watch 3 or later, as well as the Fitbit Air.

With Blood Pressure Trends, the watch will monitor blood flow using the optical heart rate sensor, as well as motion sensors. That data gets fed into an AI model to estimate the shape and speed of pulse waves traveling under the skin to approximate whether your blood pressure is trending higher or lower. (There will be no direct systolic or diastolic measurements.)

While we’ve seen other wearable players like Apple and Whoop tackle blood pressure insights, Google’s attempt at non-invasive insulin resistance detection is brand spanking new. Insulin resistance describes a condition in which your body doesn’t metabolize food effectively. The pancreas has to produce more insulin to utilize blood glucose, and untreated, it often leads to fatigue, stubborn weight gain, and eventually, Type 2 diabetes. This feature would passively estimate whether your insulin resistance is trending higher or lower month to month based on signals like heart rhythm, sleep quality, and daily movements. To validate the algorithm, Google says it tested the algorithm against blood draws and published its findings in a peer-reviewed study in Nature .

Again, this is not noninvasive blood glucose monitoring. As with Blood Pressure Trends, there are no direct readings involved, and this isn’t a screening feature for diabetes. It’s just flagging when your lifestyle trends indicate sustained metabolic stress over a monthlong period. Even so, I’ve spilled a ton of ink on the decadelong process for me to get diagnosed with insulin resistance. It can remain asymptomatic for several years, it may not show up in routine metabolic tests, and a traditional diagnosis involves nagging doctors to test fasting insulin and glucose via blood draws. We’ll have to see how this feature works in real life, but it’s potentially huge if it works well.

items.content:
﻿The Quick Share update makes it easier to share contact info and files between Pixel devices, and soon, Samsung phones.

Android’s AirDrop-like Quick Share feature will now let some devices exchange files and contact information when tapped together. The update is coming to Pixel 6 series phones and newer starting today, according to Google’s announcement , and will roll out to Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra , Fold 8 , and Flip 8 “soon.”

The tap-to-share feature uses NFC and proximity to simplify sharing, enabling users to wirelessly send contact details, photos, videos, and more by opening the share sheet menu and bringing the two devices close together. Quick Share’s tapping update will also be expanded to “more Android devices by the end of the year,” according to Google, but no device models were specified.

items.title: The Pixel Tag is Google’s answer to the AirTag
items.summary: More than two years after launching its own device-tracking network, Google has finally followed up with its own tracker. The Pixel Tag, which goes on sale in November, looks like one of the more capable trackers too: It combines ultra wideband (UWB) with Bluetooth 6.0 Channel So
items.content:
The $29 tracker combines UWB with Bluetooth channel sounding.

Photography by David Imel / The Verge

More than two years after launching its own device-tracking network, Google has finally followed up with its own tracker. The Pixel Tag, which goes on sale in November, looks like one of the more capable trackers too: It combines ultra wideband (UWB) with Bluetooth 6.0 Channel Sounding for two distinct types of precision tracking.

The Pixel Tag goes on sale on November 11th, unlike the newly announced Pixel 11 and Pixel Watch 5 , which are already available to preorder and ship next week. When it arrives, the Tag will cost $29, with a four-pack for $99 — the exact same pricing as Apple’s AirTag 2 .

The Pixel Tag is a slim oblong device available in one grayish color — Fog — that weighs about 12g, or 0.4oz. Like the AirTag, it has no built-in hooks or clips for attaching to objects you want to track. There’s a single button that will trigger a sound on your phone, for the rare occasion when you’ve got the Tag but have lost your main device. It also has an IP67 rating, so it should be safe from dust and rain. As for the battery, the Pixel Tag takes CR2032 coin batteries, and says one battery should last for over a year.

Naturally, it’ll be compatible with Google’s Find Hub network , which leverages the Bluetooth capabilities of Android devices worldwide to help locate lost objects. After a rocky launch, the network has improved steadily since, though when I tested it last year I found it was still less precise than Apple’s.

Once you’re close enough to the Pixel Tag, UWB lets the Find Hub app display the distance and direction to the tracker, so long as you’re using a phone with a UWB chip. Channel Sounding is a newer development that can display the exact distance, but not direction, and it will work with any phone or tablet that includes Bluetooth 6.0 . The Moto Tag 2 is the only other tracker to currently support it.

Google device owners will need a Pixel 10 or later to take advantage of Channel Sounding, and any Pro model since the 6 for UWB — even in the new Pixel 11 series, the base model still lacks UWB. You can track the Tag using a Pixel Watch too, and any model since the 4 will support Channel Sounding, while the 2 or later include UWB. You can also ask Gemini to ring the Tag’s speaker for you.

items.title: 4 New Camera Tricks on Google’s Latest Pixel 11 Smartphones
items.summary: From Magic Capture and Instant Night Sight to a built-in teleprompter, here’s a look at a few camera features on Google’s new Pixel 11 series.
items.content:
Google's Pixel Camera chief, Isaac Reynolds, thinks year-to-year upgrades to smartphone cameras are still critical , even though some detractors think they’re passé.

“A person who is a casual photographer and desperately wants to be a hobbyist—they're never going to break that ceiling unless you give them the tools," he says. "The features that others call ‘meh’—for some people, those features are life-changing."

Take the 30X Super Res Zoom on the Pixel 7 Pro from 2022, which uses machine learning to stitch together multiple frames in a digitally zoomed photo to give you a result that’s much sharper than you're used to. Reynolds says that because of this feature, Google now sees people using 30X zoom dramatically more than before.

The new Pixel 11 Pro, announced today , can zoom up to 120X, though in addition to the digital stitching, it relies on AI-generated pixels to fill in some details. Reynolds says maybe having that capability is enough to get someone interested in, say, wildlife photography. After experimenting on their phone, they’d be ready to invest in a professional camera and a big zoom lens.

“There's a reason I work on low light and zoom every single year," he says. "Because no matter how much I do it, when I do the user study with thousands of respondents, people always want more."

For the Pixel 11 series, Google has demonstrated a handful of upgrades that can drastically alter the look of your photos, and even take some of the work out of capturing photos. Here's a closer look at a few top new camera capabilities on the Pixel 11 series.

So you want to capture a video of an important event—a concert of your favorite band, singing happy birthday to a loved one as a waiter brings a cake over, or your kid's recital. Too often, you see people holding their phone up during these milestones, trying to capture the moment, instead of being present. That's the problem Google's new Magic Capture feature is trying to solve.

This is a new mode that sits next to the Photo/Video tab in the Pixel camera app. Select Magic Capture, and it will kick off a two-minute video recording. Then, rather than keeping the phone planted in front of your face, hold or prop the phone up so it’s pointing at your subject, then ignore the phone. The idea is to let Google's Gemini artificial intelligence models capture the scene and take photos on your behalf, so you can actually pay attention to what's happening in front of you.

The result? You'll get access to the full video (it's restricted to 1080p, but anyone with a Pixel 11 Pro can use Google's Video Boost technology to bump that to 4K). More important is the handful of photos you'll get—in full quality—as if you tapped on the shutter button yourself during the best moments. Reynolds says Gemini does a remarkable job of identifying “peak” occurrences in the scene, analyzing more than 500 frames to find perfect shots you'll want in your photo library.

I gave it a whirl during a demo with some live dancers. Indeed, all I had to do was hold the phone to the side—not in my face—and after the dance was over, I looked at the camera roll and found some surprisingly well-composed shots. It even cropped images with light edits based on what Gemini thought was a better composition. It's very much reminiscent of Google's Clips , a 2018 camera that ultimately flopped but similarly used AI to capture family moments. Magic Capture feels more intentional, and perhaps more useful.

“I do think the dream is: ‘I don’t have to deal with it; AI can look at a hundred times as many frames as I can, let the models handle this,'” Reynolds says. “That is sort of the dream of so many people who refuse to take their phones out at an event because they don't want their kid to remember their face hidden behind a camera.”

Everyone knows that if you want to shoot a photo in low light, you have to stay as still as possible. Our smartphone cameras take a few seconds to capture multiple images and stitch them together, meaning small movements can end in a blurry mess. But Google says its new Tensor G6 processor on the Pixel 11 Pro and Pixel 11 Pro XL can alleviate this problem by enabling a feature called Instant Night Sight.

Instant Night Sight is 4.5 times faster than the standard Night Sight available on other Pixel phones. Yes, that means there will still be a small shutter delay as the camera captures the photo, but the delay isn’t as pronounced as before. Much of this is thanks to new image-processing models tailored for the G6 chipset, which are bolstered by engine updates to Night Sight.

There are also hardware upgrades to a few cameras on the Pixel 11 series that provide greater light sensitivity, delivering brighter images in low light. Specifically, the Pixel 11 and Pixel 11 Pro Fold have an upgraded 48-megapixel primary camera that absorbs 56 percent more light, and the new 48-megapixel telephoto camera on the Pixel 11 Pro has 30 percent more light sensitivity. It's a shame Instant Night Sight is only available to the two Pro candybar Pixels.

Like Apple is doing with its Photographic Styles, Google is ceding more control to you, the photographer, in how your photos look. The Pixel Camera now features “Camera Looks,” and there are four main pillars: Original, Natural, Shadows, and Vanilla. Natural offers “relaxed details,” whereas Vanilla has a warm, golden glow; Shadow nets you deeper contrast. These aren't just filters like the ones you slap on Instagram—they're calibrated at the sensor level, and you can see what they look like in the camera viewfinder before you tap the shutter button.

From there, you can swipe left to cycle through a handful of additional looks, like Digi, Black Tie, Minimal, Editorial, Classic, and Velvet. And within each of these, you can further customize the settings for things like brightness, contrast, and highlights to tailor the look to your taste.

items.title: Google Pixel 11 Series, Pixel Watch 5, Pixel Tag: Specs, Features, Price, Release Date
items.summary: The Pixel 11 smartphone lineup is here, alongside the Pixel Watch 5 and the all-new Pixel Tag.
items.content:
Google is dialing things up to 11 this year with its Pixel phones . Ahead of its annual Made by Google event in New York City, the company unwrapped the Pixel 11 smartphone family—which includes the Pixel 11, Pixel 11 Pro, Pixel 11 Pro XL, and Pixel 11 Pro Fold—alongside the Pixel Watch 5 smartwatch . There's also a new hardware addition: the Pixel Tag, which seems designed to be the AirTag of the Android world.

Here's everything you need to know about the hardware changes and software upgrades on Google’s latest devices. Preorders open today, and the phones and watches go on sale August 20.

The Pixel 11 starts with 256 GB of storage and comes in an eye-popping Hibiscus color.

It was inevitable, but prices are up across the board for Google's Pixel 11 series. The Pixel 11 now starts at $899, and on the highest end of the spectrum, the Pixel 11 Pro Fold is now $1,900. This means both devices got $100 price bumps. There's some good news: Google has bumped the base storage up to 256 GB on every device, a move matching Samsung 's and Apple's latest handsets .

One big design change across the entire Pixel 11 series is on the oval camera bar on the back—it's now an all-glass surface, as opposed to a mix of metal and glass on its predecessors. Google says the camera bar on the Pixel 11 is more than 40 percent thinner, and when you pop on Google's case, the camera bar disappears and is completely flush. The Pixel 11 has the most striking color of the lot—Hibiscus—joined by more muted Pistachio, Frost, and Obsidian.

The Pixel 11 and Pixel 11 Pro Fold share more in common than you'd expect. They now have the same primary 48-megapixel camera, upgraded this year with a larger sensor that can capture up to 56 percent more light for brighter low-light images. The 10.8-megapixel telephoto camera, which has a 5X optical zoom, can now digitally zoom up to 30X. At these higher digital zoom levels, Google's machine learning algorithm puts in the work to clean up the digital noise and deliver an enhanced photo.

Google's folding phone is now 10 percent lighter and 1 mm thinner than the Pixel 10 Pro Fold , with slimmer bezels around the screen, though the phone is still heftier and thicker than Samsung's new Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra . It maintains its IP68 dust- and water-resistance rating, but there's a new glass-fiber composite back cover that Google says is “nearly impossible to crack” and an upgraded hinge that better protects the inner display from accidental drops. All of this, Google claims, makes the device three times more durable than its predecessor . Bold words.

The Pixel 11 Pro Fold is slightly lighter and thinner and is supposedly three times more durable than its predecessor.

The Fold features HiLight, a glowing LED on the back (excluded on the Pixel 11 but available on the Pixel 11 Pro phones). It lights up when you talk to Gemini, much like the glowing lights on the new Google Home Speaker . You can set it to light up in specific colors when you receive phone calls from your favorite contacts. Google says it's exploring the same capability for text messages, but didn't comment on whether it will enable HiLight for other notifications.

Both phones have been upgraded to 25-watt wireless charging speeds for faster Qi2 charging.

HiLight, the glowing light, is exclusive to the Pixel 11 Pro, Pixel 11 Pro XL, and Pixel 11 Pro Fold.

Even if the Pixel 11 Pro Fold has “Pro” in its name, a few extra upgrades in the candybar Pixel 11 Pro and Pixel 11 Pro XL elevate them to be the best hardware and software from Google. Both share the same specs outside of screen size, battery size, and charging speeds. They also are seeing $100 price bumps to $1,100 and $1,300, respectively.

The new colors this year are Canyon, Olive, and Fog, but the standard Obsidian (aka black) now has an all-matte finish. The same HiLight glowing LED as on the Fold is on the all-glass camera bar (Google is also bringing back the “Glowbar” on its upcoming Googlebook laptops later this year, so these glowing lights are a big theme for 2026). There's a new anti-scratch display coating that purportedly delivers more than double the scratch resistance of the Pixel 10 Pro.

Google says the main camera for the Pixel 11 Pro and 11 Pro XL has been upgraded to a new 50-megapixel sensor, and there's a new 48-megapixel telephoto camera that Google claims has 30 percent better light sensitivity. The Pro line now uses this camera for its Pro Zoom feature , which uses generative AI to fill in the gaps of ultra-zoomed-in photos, allowing you to zoom up to 120X compared to 100X on last year's devices.

Thanks to the Tensor G6 chip, there's a big upgrade to Night Sight, Google's low-light photo mode. Exclusive to these two devices, it's now 4.5 times faster and dubbed “Instant Night Sight.” That means your subject won't have to stay super still in dim conditions while the phone captures the shot—it's a little more forgiving. That upgraded image signal processor on the chip also unlocks 4K portrait video for the first time. (It was capped at 1080p before.)

These two Pro Pixels are still the only ones in the lineup to support Google's Video Boost technology . If enabled, your video clips are uploaded and processed on Google's servers to improve brightness and colors, reduce noise, and upgrade stabilization. This year, they'll now be treated to “Pro Stable Video” as well. It will automatically activate for shaky scenes and deliver super-stable footage. Samsung and Apple have been delivering on that front largely through hardware, but it's no surprise that Google's leveraging its software expertise instead.

AI 기반 사이버 보안 및 IT 인프라 통합 플랫폼 기업 위드네트웍스(대표 안종업 )가 11~12일 서울 코엑스에서 열린 'ISEC 2026(제20회 국제 시큐리티 콘퍼런스)'에 참가, AI 기반 자산·취약점 통합 관리 플랫폼 ' withVTM' 신규 버전 을 처음 공개했다. 이 제품은 실제 인프라를 3D 가상 공간에 그대로 재현하는 '보안 디지털 트윈'을 적용했다.

12일 회사에 따르면, 'AI로 구현하는 자율보안의 미래'를 주제로 열린 이번 행사에서 'AI가 취약점을 쏟아내는 미토스 시대'를 화두로 제시하고, N2SF·ISMS-P 대응을 위한 지속적 위협 노출 관리(CTEM) 체계와 이를 구현한 'withVTM'을 전면에 내세웠다.

AI가 스스로 취약점을 탐지하는 '미토스 쇼크' 이후 공격 표면 관리의 기준이 근본적으로 달라졌다. 또 AI 기술 확산으로 공격은 빠르고 정교해지는 동시에 공격 범위도 확대되고 있으나, 이에 대응할 보안 인력과 예산은 한정돼 있다. 위드네트웍스는 이러한 비대칭 환경에서 조직이 증명해야 할 지표는 처리한 취약점 건수가 아니라 실제 위험 수준을 얼마나 신속하게 낮췄는지라고 보고, 전체 취약점을 일괄 점검하는 기존 방식 대신 외부에 실제로 노출된 위험부터 처리하는 '지속적 위협 노출 관리(CTEM)'로의 전환을 제시했다.

위드네트웍스는 실제 위험이 단일 취약점이 아니라 여러 약점의 '조합'에서 발생한다는 점에 주목했다. 외부에 노출된 API와 불필요한 개방 포트, SBOM 내 취약 라이브러리, 기본 계정과 과도한 접근 권한, 민감 데이터 접근 경로가 하나의 자산에서 겹치면 개별 취약점 점수가 낮더라도 악용 가능성은 급격히 상승한다.

개별 취약점 단위로 산정되는 CVSS(Common Vulnerability Scoring system) 점수만으로는 이러한 조합 위험이 드러나지 않는다. 'withVTM'은 취약점 점수 하나로 위험을 판단하지 않는다. 자산 중요도와 외부 노출 현황, KEV·EPSS 등 실제 악용 신호, 설정 결함과 권한 상태를 자산 단위로 결합해 AI 기반 위험 등급으로 환산하고, 개별 점수는 낮지만 결합 시 악용 가능성이 높아지는 자산을 우선 조치 대상으로 제시한다.

한편 디지털 트윈은 실제 설비나 공간을 가상 환경에 동일하게 복제하고 상태를 실시간으로 동기화해 변화를 검증하는 기술로, 제조와 도시·시설 관리 분야에서 먼저 상용화됐다. 보안 영역에 적용하면 운영 환경에 영향을 주지 않고 자산 구성과 연결 관계를 검증할 수 있으며, 자산 목록만으로는 확인되지 않는 연결 구조와 외부 노출 지점을 단일 화면에서 파악하는 효과를 얻을 수 있다.

위드네트웍스는 이 기술을 IT 자산·취약점 관리에 적용해 이번 'withVTM' 신규 버전에 3D 보안 디지털 트윈으로 구현했다. 국내에서 디지털 트윈을 IT 자산·취약점 관리에 적용한 상용 사례는 위드네트웍스가 처음이라고 회사는 강조했다.

'withVTM'의 3D 보안 디지털 트윈은 실제 자산과 네트워크 구성을 가상 공간에 그대로 재현한다. 점검 시점마다 새로 작성되는 목록이 아니라 상시 동기화되는 단일 환경에서 조직 전체를 조망하는 방식이다. 자산 식별 단위도 서버·IP에 한정되지 않는다. 서비스와 API, 컨테이너, SBOM 구성요소까지 분해해 공격 표면 전반을 반영하며, 자산 목록에 등재된 적 없는 섀도우 IT와 미관리 자산도 동일한 화면에서 확인된다.

자산별 AI 기반 위험 등급은 3D 화면에 그대로 표시돼 우선 조치 대상이 즉시 식별된다. 자산과 취약점의 관계, 자산 간 연결 관계가 함께 매핑되므로 특정 취약점이 어느 자산에 존재하고 해당 자산이 어떤 자산·서비스와 연결돼 있는지 화면에서 추적할 수 있다. 신규 도입 자산과 미관리 자산, 신규 공개 취약점은 식별되는 즉시 디지털 트윈에 반영돼 정기 점검 주기 사이에 발생하던 가시성 공백을 해소한다. 표와 보고서로 분산돼 있던 자산·취약점 관리를 단일 화면 기반의 상시 관리 체계로 전환한 것이 이번 버전의 핵심 변화다.

또 'withVTM'은 3D 보안 디지털 트윈을 중심으로 전사 자산 통합 가시성, 섀도우 IT·API 관리, SBOM 공급망 보안, CVE·CCE 상시 점검, AI 기반 위험 우선순위, AI 디펜스 데이터셋, 보안 운영 자동화, N2SF C·S·O 등급 관리, 감사·컴플라이언스 대응까지 하나의 운영 체계로 연결한다. 식별·분석·판단·조치·검증·증적 여섯 단계가 단절 없이 이어지며, 점검·조치 이력에서 감사 증적이 자동으로 축적돼 N2SF와 ISMS·ISMS-P 인증 개편, 정보보호 실태평가 대응에 활용된다.

함께 선보인 'withREX '는 위협 노출 진단 서비스다. 에이전트를 설치하지 않아 운영 중단 없이 전사 공격 표면을 단기간에 점검하며, 자산 목록에서 누락된 자산과 외부에 개방된 API를 식별하고 노출 수준을 수치로 산출한다.

두 제품 모두 조달청 디지털서비스몰에 등록돼 공공기관이 별도 절차 없이 도입할 수 있다. 행사 첫날 부스에는 공공기관과 금융·제조 분야 보안 담당자의 방문이 이어졌다고 회사는 밝혔다. N2SF와 ISMS·ISMS-P 인증 개편 대응을 앞둔 실무자들은 자산 식별 범위와 감사 증적 확보 방안을 집중적으로 문의했다.

안종업 위드네트웍스 대표는 “보안 담당자를 가장 위태롭게 만드는 것은 알고도 못 고친 취약점이 아니라, 있는 줄도 몰랐던 자산”이라며 “빠짐없이 찾아내고, 그 자산 위에서 취약점이 어떻게 조합되는지까지 분석해 지금 무엇을 먼저 조치할지 답을 내는 것이 핵심이다. 보안 디지털 트윈은 그 판단 결과를 누구나 같은 화면에서 보게 만드는 방식”이라고 말했다. 이어 “자산과 취약점, 노출, 위협 정보를 상시로 수집해 일관되게 정규화한 데이터가 결국 AI 자율보안의 기초 자산이 될 것”이라고 덧붙였다.

items.title: Insta360’s next 360-degree action cam puts bigger sensors in a smaller design
items.summary: Insta360 announced the next iteration of its popular 360-degree action cameras that have helped the company expand its offerings. The new X6 introduces a design that's smaller than last year's X5 and X4 Air but with improved video capabilities thanks to an even larger pair of cus
items.content:
The smaller X6 comes with improved 8K recording, stronger and cheaper replacement lenses, and a battery life boost.

Insta360 announced the next iteration of its popular 360-degree action cameras that have helped the company expand its offerings . The new X6 introduces a design that’s smaller than last year’s X5 and X4 Air but with improved video capabilities thanks to an even larger pair of custom 1/1.1-inch square sensors from Sony. While last year’s models offered 8K recording at up to 30fps, the new X6 can capture 8K at up to 50fps. It also carries forward the X5’s replaceable lenses, which are now five times more scratch-resistant and 60 percent cheaper, according to the company.

The Insta360 X6 is available today in black or white through the company’s online store and other retailers starting at $699.99, which is $150 more expensive than last year’s $549.99 X5. It’s also available as part of a $799.99 Essentials Bundle that adds an additional battery, an invisible selfie stick, a fast charging case, and other accessories.

The most obvious upgrade for the X6 is a smaller design that’s a little wider and thicker than the X5, but a full inch shorter and 4 grams lighter, making it more pocketable than its predecessor. Shrinking the X6 did result in a slightly smaller 2.32-inch touchscreen on the back, but while the X5 featured a 2.5-inch LCD display, the X6 gets an upgrade to OLED.

While the new X6 doesn’t feature full 1-inch sensors like the DJI Osmo 360 , its new 1/1.1-inch square sensors come very close and offer 33 percent more sensor area and “four times the light intake per frame” when compared to the 1/1.28-inch sensors in the X5. Those sensors work alongside multiple AI chips, including two dedicated to imaging, to give the X6 better low-light performance with improved denoising. It’s also the first 360-degree camera, Insta360 claims, with in-camera Dolby Vision support so that brightness and contrast metadata is captured frame by frame to ensure HDR footage looks accurate on supported displays.

When capturing 360-degree footage using both cameras the X6 maxes out at 8K/50fps, but you can boost that to as high as 6K/120fps or 4K/240fps in a “Bullet Time” mode designed for capturing slow-motion footage. You can use the X6 as a 2D action camera by recording with just one sensor at a time, but that’s limited to a maximum resolution of 5K/60fps, or 120fps if you drop to 4K. Still photography with the X6 is also getting an upgrade to 120 megapixels when capturing 360-degree images, or 42 megapixels when using just one side of the camera.

Despite the camera being smaller, Insta360 managed to squeeze a slightly larger 2,600mAh battery into the X6 that the company claims will keep it recording up to 51 percent longer than the X5, which came with a 2,400mAh battery. The X6 will record for around 140 minutes at 8K/30fps before it dies, but you can extend that with the optional X6 Power Selfie Stick accessory, which adds an extra 180 minutes of runtime.

Other upgrades include improved waterproofing to a depth of 66 feet and a better invisible dive case that can be used to film underwater as deep as 60 meters without the case itself showing up in footage.

Insta360 has also upgraded the InstaFrame feature introduced with the X5 that can produce a social media-friendly flat 4K video without requiring any manual editing by tracking and focusing on people, pets, or other subjects in frame. For those who don’t want to edit 360-degree footage either, a new feature called PanoMind uses an AI model trained on 10,000 hours of 360-degree footage to automatically create a highlight reel from footage on the camera while the X6 is charging.

36개국 2025년 사이버범죄 동향 분석…피해액 전년 대비 2배 이상 증가

컴퓨팅 입력 :2026/08/12 21:34

에스투더블유(S2W)가 최근 인터폴(INTERPOL)이 공개한 ‘2026 아프리카 사이버위협 평가 보고서(African Cyberthreat Assessment Report 2026)’ 제작에 민간 부문 파트너로 참여했다. 아프리카 사이버범죄 동향 분석을 위한 데이터와 인텔리전스를 제공했다.

12일 회사에 따르면, 이번 보고서는 영국 외무·영연방·개발부(FCDO) 지원으로 추진한 ‘아프리카 사이버범죄 공동 작전(AFJOC)’ 일환으로 발간됐다. 아프리카 36개 인터폴 회원국의 법 집행기관이 제공한 설문 데이터를 토대로 S2W, 마스터카드(Mastercard), 포티넷(Fortinet), 섀도서버재단(Shadowserver Foundation), 트렌드AI(TrendAI) 등 글로벌 기업 및 비영리 단체의 텔레메트리 데이터(Telemetry Data)와 위협 인텔리전스(TI)를 결합한 다출처 분석 방식으로 작성했다.

보고서에 따르면 아프리카에서 집계된 사이버범죄 관련 피해액은 2024년 1억9200만 달러에서 2025년 4억8400만 달러로 두 배 이상 늘었다. 확인된 피해자 수는 같은 기간 3만5000명에서 8만7000명으로 증가했다. 또 2025년 아프리카에서 보고된 사이버범죄의 55%에는 AI가 일정 수준 활용된 것으로 조사됐으며, 피싱 캠페인 자동화와 딥페이크 기반 사칭, 금융 사기를 위한 합성 신원 생성 등에 악용되며 공격의 속도와 규모, 정교함을 높인 주요 수법으로 꼽혔다.

인터폴의 ‘게이트웨이 이니셔티브(Gateway Initiative)’ 한국 유일 파트너인 S2W는 이번 보고서 제작 과정에서 AI 기반 빅데이터 수집·분석 기술을 활용해 다크웹 포럼의 아프리카 출처 콘텐츠를 식별·분류하고, 전년 대비 62% 증가한 사실을 확인했다. 해당 콘텐츠에는 신분증과 SIM 카드 PIN, 은행 계정 인증 정보, 모바일 금융 계정 정보 등이 다수 포함됐다. 이 가운데 상당수는 과거 침해 사고와 피싱 캠페인, 침해된 모바일 애플리케이션을 통해 유출된 정보로 파악됐다.

아프리카의 사이버위협은 역내 피해에 그치지 않고, 초국가적 범죄 네트워크를 통해 다른 국가로 확산되고 있다. 보고서는 서아프리카를 아프리카와 글로벌 범죄 생태계를 잇는 연결 지점으로 평가했으며, 국가정보원도 2025년 나이지리아 기반 국제 마약 조직이 로맨스 스캠(Romance Scam)으로 한국인 등을 마약 운반책으로 포섭한 사례를 공개했다. 이처럼 온라인 사기 수법이 마약 유통 등 다른 범죄와 결합하고 범죄망이 국경을 넘어 확장되는 상황에서 국가 간 정보 공유는 물론 민간 기업의 데이터·기술과 연계해 범죄 인프라를 조기에 식별하고 차단하는 민관 공조 체계의 중요성도 커졌다.

닐 제튼(Neal Jetton) 인터폴 사이버범죄국장은 “사이버범죄는 아프리카 지역에서 가장 중대한 위협 중 하나로 부상했다. AI는 사전 정찰과 피싱부터 협박과 추적 회피에 이르기까지, 사이버공격의 전 단계를 자동화한다”라며 “그러나 국가 간 협력을 통해 사이버범죄 인프라를 식별하고, 무력화하며, 해체할 수 있다는 사실 역시 확인하고 있다”라고 말했다.

서상덕 S2W 대표는 “S2W는 인프라와 제도적 기반이 충분히 갖춰지지 않아 사이버공격에 상대적으로 취약한 개발도상국의 범죄 실태를 면밀히 분석하고, 각국 법 집행기관이 치안 공백을 메우는 데 실질적으로 활용할 수 있는 양질의 인텔리전스를 제공하는 데 주력해 왔다”면서 “앞으로도 AI 기반의 글로벌 데이터 수집 및 분석 기술을 지속 고도화해 세계 각지에서 발생하는 안보 위협의 신호를 신속하게 포착, 초국가적 범죄 대응을 지원하겠다"고 밝혔다.

items.title: Honor’s Robot Phone is better than a gimbal in a phone has any right to be
items.summary: The Robot Phone, which launches today in China, doesn't sound like a good idea - and not only because it's not actually a robot. Instead it's a regular Android smartphone with its main camera installed on a compact gimbal arm that unfolds from the phone's rear. Cramming the equiv
items.content:
After an hour of testing the Robot Phone, I’m surprised but impressed.

The Robot Phone, which launches today in China, doesn’t sound like a good idea — and not only because it’s not actually a robot. Instead it’s a regular Android smartphone with its main camera installed on a compact gimbal arm that unfolds from the phone’s rear. Cramming the equivalent of a DJI Osmo Pocket inside a smartphone sounds like a great way to get the worst of both worlds, but after an hour of testing, I’m cautiously optimistic that Honor has made this Frankenphone work.

This is a smaller gimbal than you’ll find on DJI’s compact Osmo Pocket line — Honor claims it’s the smallest in the world. It still makes the phone bulkier than normal, at 9.6mm thick (not counting the chunky camera section itself) and weighing 248g. Only the Samsung and Huawei trifolds are bigger, and my first impression was that the phone felt oddly dated as a result, despite the cutting-edge camera inside.

The gimbal camera will spend most of its life tucked inside the phone’s camera module, protected by a small plastic screen. Even folded away, the 200-megapixel, 1/1.28-inch-type sensor serves as the phone’s main camera, joined by a 200-megapixel periscope telephoto and a 50-megapixel ultrawide.

But the real fun comes when the camera arm unfurls. First, you slide the plastic screen off — manually — so it covers the phone’s other two cameras instead. Then, activate the gimbal through the software, and it springs into action. (If you try to activate the gimbal without sliding away the cover, the phone won’t let you.)

Having the gimbal makes it easier to take selfies using the more powerful main camera, shoot at odd angles while keeping the display head-on, and record video with smooth panning and tracking. You control it using the phone’s default camera app, which offers simple controls in its photo and video tabs, and more complex options in a dedicated pro video section. Honor has also thrown in the fun option to take a panoramic selfie, the gimbal spinning around to take multiple photos and stitch them together.

The 3-axis gimbal has nearly 360 degrees of movement and a variety of tracking modes, including FPV, spin shot, super steady, and subject-tracking that can detect people as well as objects (and works in video calls too, though I’m not sure if anything beyond Weibo is supported). There are no additional physical controls, so you have to use an onscreen joystick for manual adjustments, which is a little finicky compared to dedicated hardware. Then again, the 6.3-inch phone screen is a much easier way to navigate settings and menus than an Osmo Pocket’s tiny display.

That’s helpful since Honor has packed in plenty of options. In addition to settings like resolution and frame rate, you can shoot in portrait or landscape, adjust the speed of the gimbal or the sensitivity of the joystick, switch aspect ratio, and toggle focus peaking on the display. Thanks to Honor’s partnership with camera company Arri, you can also record in a variety of different film-inspired looks, along with Arri’s own LogC3 format.

An hour wasn’t enough time to fully assess the gimbal’s performance, but I did get a sense. Video felt a little less stable than I’m used to from this year’s Osmo Pocket 4, but not by much, which is impressive given how much smaller the setup is. A few minutes of sustained recording is enough to make the whole phone get pretty hot, but that’s true of DJI’s gimbal cameras too.

I have a quick clip of test footage from my time with the phone, showing some simple panning from the main camera mode’s virtual joystick — I would have recorded something more exciting, but I wasn’t expecting to be allowed to publish the footage!

Photos seem to benefit from the gimbal too. The stabilization can help keep the camera steady between the multiple exposures that modern phones routinely stitch together for every photo you take. It was a bright, sunny day when I tested the phone, but when I stepped into a nearby church, it did an impressive job with the dimmer room and backlit stained glass windows. Between the fairly large sensor and the extra stabilization, this could be one of the better phones around for photos in dark conditions.

Still, there are obvious reasons not to buy the Robot Phone. The first is that you probably can’t: Honor is only launching it in China, and has said it has no plans to release it elsewhere. That might change in a future iteration.

Honor also wouldn’t tell me ahead of time how much the phone will cost, but I’m going to go ahead and guess it’ll be more than simply buying a good phone and a separate Osmo Pocket, or the cheaper (if bulkier) option of a standalone gimbal to hold your phone . That’s the classic foldable problem too (it’s like a phone plus a tablet for substantially more than the cost of both!). You’ll have to be willing to pay a real premium to combine those two gadgets into one. The benefits may be worth it for some, like livestreamers who want to be able to shoot stable smartphone video and stream it directly, but most people would likely be better served by separate products.

The biggest concern is durability though. Honor says the phone has an IP54 rating for protection and dust and water when the camera is fully stowed, but that doesn’t apply when the gimbal is raised. Even closed, this is a little less tough than other flagship phones. That’s true of dedicated gimbal cameras too, but those aren’t likely to be exposed to potential damage nearly as often as your smartphone. Factor in the added risk of damage from drops, the potential for anything with moving parts to go wrong, and the presumably prohibitive cost of any repairs that fall outside Honor’s one-year warranty, and the Robot Phone is a big gamble for anyone to buy.

Do the tradeoffs make sense? For me, probably not. For some professional content creators, maybe.

items.content:
You hear it often: Smartphones have plateaued . A small boost to battery life here, a minor camera upgrade there—our glass slabs don't seem to change all that much from year to year.

That's exactly the kind of sentiment Honor wants to counter with the Robot Phone, which has a motorized camera that pops up out of the top. Honor has been teasing the phone since late 2025 .

On Wednesday, the company officially made the Robot Phone available to buyers in China. Honor was originally a subsidiary of Huawei , but it's now a wholly independent company. While its Android phones are available in regions like the UK, Europe, Africa, and Latin America, it has no presence in the US, and the Robot Phone remains a China-exclusive for now . (Pricing is yet to be confirmed.)

Honor calls the Robot Phone a “new species of smartphone,” one designed to cater to the needs of the modern mobile content creator. That's the thinking behind its nifty trick of a gimbal-powered camera embedded in the phone, which makes it a potentially more enticing option for filming videos compared to dedicated gimbal cameras like the DJI Osmo Pocket or the Insta360 Luna Ultra .

Building that roving eye was no small feat. Honor says it had to develop the micro-motor for the gimbal itself because off-the-shelf components were too large, reducing the volume by 65 percent compared to traditional gimbals on the market. Honor claims the titanium-alloy gimbal motor weighs just 2.6 grams. It's embedded in a 6.3-inch smartphone that's only 9.59 mm thick (for reference, the iPhone 17 Pro is 8.75 mm).

The Honor Robot Phone and its 200-megapixel gimbal camera.

The gimbal-powered 200-megapixel camera isn't the only camera, either. It's joined by a 200-megapixel telephoto camera and a 50-megapixel ultrawide, not to mention the 50-megapixel selfie shooter. The gimbal has 4 degrees of freedom, and you can activate it in the camera app or by making a palm motion on the selfie camera. And since it can rotate 300 degrees, you can use it as a selfie camera too.

The phone is shockingly light at 248 grams (the aforementioned iPhone 17 Pro is 206 grams). I wholly expected the Robot Phone to be top-heavy, with all those camera components at the top and the massive 7,060-mAh silicon-carbon battery inside powering the whole system. But in fact it’s decently balanced.

A glass cover protects the gimbal camera, and you can slide it to the right when you're ready to activate the gimbal. Once the camera is out, you can manually control the gimbal for ultra-smooth video capture through the camera app, or use preset motions to give your clips a cinematic look. There's even voice control with natural language, so you can say “turn around for 5 seconds.”

The motorized stabilization in the camera makes action shots—which can typically look shaky on traditional smartphones—look amazingly smooth. There are tracking modes as well, such as a subject tracker that keeps the selected person in the frame even as they move around. You can imagine how helpful that can be for solo travelers vlogging their way through a trip.

Some of these features extend past content creation. For example, the subject-tracking mode works in video calls, meaning you can set the phone up on a table (Honor includes a case and a magnetic stand) and the camera can follow you around. I also took a group selfie, and instead of taking a normal picture, the gimbal took three photos—left, center, and right—and stitched them like a panorama for a wide shot of everyone. Quick and seamless.

There's a less effective and quite gimmicky integration with Honor's Yoyo virtual AI assistant, where the gimbal camera acts like an enigmatic robot with a pair of eyes on the phone's screen. Ask it to dance to music, and the gimbal camera will move to the beat. It can pretend to be happy or angry, making the appropriate movements to indicate its mood. The camera also serves as the AI's eyes; ask it to describe the scene in front of you, and it'll take a peek.

Honor says the case and magnetic phone stand are included in the box.

That last bit could be useful, say, if you propped the phone up and asked the assistant to watch you assemble some furniture and point out any steps you might have missed. However, Yoyo doesn't have this kind of capability yet. Honor uses Google's Gemini assistant in markets outside of China, and if the Robot Phone rolled out elsewhere, that could be a very real integration with Gemini Live .

You're probably wondering just how durable this mechanical gimbal resting on top of the phone really is. Unlike with folding phones , which are measured in lab tests to withstand more than 500,000 folds, Honor doesn't say how much strain the gimbal's motor can endure. Instead, a company spokesperson tells WIRED the “gimbal mechanism has undergone rigorous reliability testing for repeated deployment and retraction. Its durability is designed to meet everyday usage needs throughout the expected service life of the device.” There's a built-in software feature that safeguards the gimbal from "inadvertent handling or abnormal resistance," too.

It's not the first time a phone maker has toyed with a mechanical camera. OnePlus famously had a mechanical pop-up selfie camera hidden in its OnePlus 7 Pro , offering a seamless display experience with no notch or floating pinhole camera, and its motor was rated for 300,000 cycles.

The design does sacrifice the phone’s overall water and dust resistance, given that the Robot Phone is only rated at IP54 when the camera is stowed. But Honor says not to expect the same level of protection when the gimbal is deployed, meaning you might not want to risk shooting that big romantic scene for your flick during a rainstorm.

The 200-MP gimbal camera can rotate 300 degrees.

이날 씨이랩은 자사 GPU 오케스트레이션 플랫폼 ‘ 아스트라고(AstraGo )’와 연계되는 GPU 운영 진단 새 솔루션 ‘ 아스트라몬(AstraMon )’을 공식 소개, 이를 기반으로 한 파트너 사업 전략을 공유한다.

'아스트라몬(AstraMon)'은 고객사의 GPU 사용 현황을 분석해 유휴 GPU, 대기 전력, 좀비 프로세스 등 운영 비효율 요소를 데이터로 식별하고 이를 비용 관점에서 진단할 수 있게 지원하는 솔루션이다. 고객의 GPU 자원 활용 상태를 가시화함, 운영 개선이 필요한 영역을 구체적으로 파악할 수 있게 해준다.

씨이랩은 ' 측정은 AstraMon, 최적화는 AstraGo' 라는 전략 아래 두 솔루션의 역할을 명확히 구분했다. 즉, AstraMon은 GPU 자원의 운영 상태와 비효율을 진단하고, AstraGo는 GPU 자원의 배분과 활용을 최적화해준다. 이를 통해 파트너사는 고객의 GPU 운영 현황을 데이터 기반으로 제시하고, 진단 결과를 AstraGo 도입 제안으로 연계할 수 있다.

세미나에서는 ▲AstraMon 신제품 및 AstraGo 연계 전략 ▲HPE의 Compute 인프라 동향과 플랫폼 협력 방향 ▲KAIST의 최신 AI 산업 및 하드웨어 인프라 동향 ▲씨이랩 파트너 정책 및 사업 협력 방안 등이 공유된다.

씨이랩은 이번 서밋을 기점으로 이러한 영업 모델을 리셀러 파트너 네트워크에 본격 확산할 계획이다. 단순 제품 공급을 넘어 파트너사가 고객의 GPU 인프라 문제를 진단하고 개선 방안을 제안할 수 있도록 영업 체계와 협력 기반을 강화한다는 방침이다.

윤세혁 대표는 “AI 인프라 시장이 빠르게 확대되면서 경쟁의 중심도 확보한 자원을 얼마나 효율적으로 운영하고 활용하느냐로 이동하고 있다”며 “씨이랩은 AstraMon과 AstraGo를 통해 GPU 운영 가시성과 효율성을 높이고 파트너 생태계와 함께 AI 인프라 운영의 새로운 기준을 만들어 나가겠다”고 밝혔다.

items.title: Of course the ChatGPT dog cancer vaccine spawned a startup
items.summary: Remember that much-hyped story about an Australian tech entrepreneur using ChatGPT, Grok, and other AI tools to craft a personalized cancer vaccine for his dog? Well, surprise: he's launched a startup. That entrepreneur is Paul Conyngham, who says he is launching Gamgee to offer
items.content:
The hyped AI-saved-my-dog story has reached its inevitable conclusion.

Remember that much-hyped story about an Australian tech entrepreneur using ChatGPT, Grok, and other AI tools to craft a personalized cancer vaccine for his dog ? Well, surprise: he’s launched a startup.

That entrepreneur is Paul Conyngham, who says he is launching Gamgee to offer “personalised mRNA cancer vaccines for dogs.” But his ambitions go well beyond dogs — and pets — with Gamgee’s website promising the company will harness AI and genetics to develop personalized treatments for a range of diseases and species, including humans.

At the center of Gamgee’s origin story is Rosie, Conyngham’s Staffordshire bull terrier-Shar Pei mix, who features prominently on Conyngham’s social media and the startup’s website, as well as its AI-generated anime launch video . When announcing Gamgee on X, Conyngham said “I used chatgpt + computational genomics to design a personalised mRNA cancer vaccine for her tumour. Several of her tumours shrank.”

Conyngham, who stresses on Gamgee’s website that he is “not a biologist,” credits that intervention with adding years to Rosie’s life. Gamgee’s stated mission is to do that at scale. In case the canine element is lost on its visitors, the website features a slideshow of adorable dogs alongside ages and purported cancer diagnosis to remind them “who we’re building this for.”

But as I reported for The Verge earlier this year, the science behind Rosie’s story is considerably messier than Conyngham’s neat account suggests. The exact role AI played in the endeavor wasn’t clear, and researchers said the broad claims gave the technology too much credit while minimizing the role of the humans involved. Moreover, the protocol Rosie followed made it impossible to say whether the mRNA vaccine was responsible for her improvement, since it was administered alongside another therapy.

That hasn’t stopped the idea from attracting support. The startup is backed by storied tech incubator Y Combinator and says it is recruiting for its first clinical trials in Australia, with a waitlist open everywhere else (though Conyngham says they’re “accepting cases globally.”). On a section on its website aimed at veterinarians, Gamgee touts a roughly 75 per cent tumor reduction in its “first documented case,” while promising to require less than 20 minutes of a veterinarian’s time, no new clinical workflows, and a finished “vaccine in hand” in around four weeks. The company cautions that this timeline is based on a single case and may vary. Costs aren’t disclosed on the site.

Gamgee says it’s working in collaboration with the University of Queensland and institutes at the University of New South Wales in Australia, and Conyngham encourages potential funders or study partners to reach out.

Ultimately, the company says its mission extends beyond dogs and other animals to personalized treatments for humans. For a startup built around a single dog whose improvement cannot be clearly attributed to the treatment at the core of its pitch, that’s a grand ambition.
